diagrams.title: From Loss Intake to Collected Restoration Invoice
diagrams.subtitle: Five accountable handoffs connect field evidence with job economics.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Stage numbers indicate sequence, not conversion rates. Restoration contract billings are operator revenue; total insured property value and insurer claim reserves are not.
diagrams.caption: Dispatch, photo documentation, and job-cost tracking automate handoffs without deciding coverage or negotiating policy rights.

stages.label: Qualify the loss
stages.detail: Record property address, water source or fire damage, occupancy, access authority, emergency hazards, and required contractor or remediation credentials.

stages.label: Authorize the work
stages.detail: Obtain the customer's work authorization, explain deductible responsibilities, and document payment terms without promising insurer coverage.

stages.label: Mitigate and measure
stages.detail: Assign drying equipment and responsible technicians; record temperature, relative humidity, humidity ratio, material moisture, equipment days, and dated photographs using applicable IICRC documentation practices.

stages.label: Estimate and reconcile
stages.detail: Tie quantities, labor, equipment, and supplements to actual work and supporting evidence. Route policy interpretation or claim negotiation outside contractor scope.

stages.label: Invoice and collect
stages.detail: Submit an itemized invoice, track customer and insurer remittance paths, resolve contractual scope discrepancies, and reconcile receipts against job costs without unauthorized public adjusting.

diagrams.title: A Single Restoration Inquiry Cohort
diagrams.subtitle: 120 inquiries narrow to 30 fully collected jobs at day 120.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Hypothetical cohort followed for 120 days after intake closes. Every later group is a subset of the preceding group. Counts are neither annual sales forecasts nor recognized revenue.
diagrams.caption: Separate lead qualification, completed work, and cash receipt; a paid-job count cannot substitute for earned contract revenue.

stages.label: Recorded inquiries
stages.detail: Log every unique loss inquiry with source, address, contact permission, and incident date; remove duplicate calls concerning the same property and event.

stages.label: Qualified opportunities
stages.detail: Retain jobs inside the service radius with appropriate credentials, accessible premises, available capacity, and a customer able to authorize work.

stages.label: Authorized jobs
stages.detail: Count only executed work authorizations with a defined scope and payment terms; insurer acknowledgment alone does not create customer authorization.

stages.label: Completed and invoiced
stages.detail: Require completed contracted scope, supporting job records, and an issued invoice; twelve authorized jobs remain outside this completed subset.

stages.label: Fully collected jobs
stages.detail: Require cleared payment against the full outstanding invoice balance; six completed jobs remain unpaid or partially paid at the observation cutoff.

diagrams.title: Base-Case Gross Billings to Owner Net Profit
diagrams.subtitle: $1,500,000 revenue less $1,305,000 costs leaves $195,000.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Annual USD. First bar is opening revenue; four negative bars are cost deductions; the sixth bar is the closing total, not an additional cash inflow. Cost allocations are illustrative; canonical scenario revenue and net profit remain fixed.
diagrams.caption: Conservative: $500,000 × 8% = $40,000 with 2 FT + 2 C. Base: $1,500,000 × 13.0% = $195,000 with 2 FT + 2 C. Scaled: $2,500,000 × 18% = $450,000 with 3 FT + 3 C.

stages.label: Gross restoration billings
stages.detail: Recognized restoration contract revenue includes subcontracted work and materials. Do not substitute total claim value, property value, or cash advances.

stages.label: Subcontractors and materials
stages.detail: Charge actual contractor invoices and consumed materials to jobs. The 2 FT + 2 C core pod includes two individual contractor seats, not employee salaries. External vendor and trade sub-crews are charged to direct subcontractor/COGS pass-through and are not included in internal pod headcount.

stages.label: Employee payroll and burden
stages.detail: Illustrative loaded annual payroll for the two full-time seats in the 2 FT + 2 C core pod averages $135,000 per FT seat, including the working owner-manager seat where applicable.

stages.label: Field operating costs
stages.detail: Allocate vehicle operation, equipment depreciation or rental, maintenance, consumables, and field safety costs without repeating direct material charges.

stages.label: Administrative operating costs
stages.detail: Allocate facilities, insurance, dispatch software, estimating subscriptions, bookkeeping, marketing, and collection losses. Payroll, field, and administrative costs total $42,500 monthly, excluding variable direct costs.

stages.label: Annual owner net profit
stages.detail: Subtract all four cost groups from gross revenue: $1,500,000 − $795,000 − $270,000 − $105,000 − $135,000 = $195,000. This is profit, not available cash before receivable collection.

diagrams.title: Compare Job Contribution Before Fixed Operating Costs
diagrams.subtitle: Five illustrative service and payment-path combinations.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Numeric values are hypothetical contribution percentages: billings less job-variable costs, divided by billings. They are not observed market averages, net margins, or an annual service mix; do not add the percentages.
diagrams.caption: Use actual job-cost records to replace these planning inputs. The canonical Base-Case net margin remains 13.0% after all costs.

stages.label: Clean-water mitigation
stages.detail: Customer-authorized extraction and drying with itemized equipment days; customer payment or insurer remittance must be reconciled to the same contract balance.

stages.label: Fire and smoke cleaning
stages.detail: Document affected surfaces, cleaning methods, and contents handling; disputed cleaning scope can delay collection despite completed field labor.

stages.label: Mold remediation
stages.detail: Use required remediation credentials and project protocols; customer-funded work remains collectible under its contract even when coverage is excluded.

stages.label: Storm stabilization
stages.detail: Separate emergency protection from permanent repair; weather exposure, access equipment, and crew travel can erode initially attractive invoice yields.

stages.label: Reconstruction
stages.detail: Align progress invoices with completed milestones; mortgage-servicer endorsements, retainage, and trade rework can extend the cash conversion cycle.

diagrams.title: Four Checks Before Dispatch or Scope Expansion
diagrams.subtitle: Proceed only through applicable, documented operating requirements.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Numbers identify sequential decisions rather than risk scores. A failed check routes to the corrective action in its detail. Texas citations are jurisdiction-specific examples, not nationwide contractor rules.
diagrams.caption: Coverage uncertainty does not authorize contractor claim negotiation, deductible concessions, or unsafe mobilization.

stages.label: Credentials match the work?
stages.detail: Verify local contractor requirements and applicable remediation licensing, including Texas Occupations Code Chapter 1958 where relevant. If credentials are missing, exclude the work or use a properly qualified provider under a permitted contracting arrangement.

stages.label: Activity stays within contractor scope?
stages.detail: Under Texas Insurance Code sections 4102.051 and 4102.163, assess licensing and contractor restrictions before any adjusting activity. Explain construction quantities and prices; redirect coverage advocacy or settlement negotiation to an authorized professional.

stages.label: Payment terms preserve required deductibles?
stages.detail: Review Texas Business and Commerce Code section 27.02 where applicable. Reject prohibited deductible waivers, disguised rebates, and inflated invoices; document the customer's actual payment obligations and collection path.

stages.label: Hazards and cash exposure controlled?
stages.detail: Apply 29 CFR 1910.134 when respiratory protection is required, 29 CFR 1926.1101 for covered asbestos work, and 40 CFR 745.85 for covered renovations. Assign qualified crews, protective measures, and funded job commitments before releasing affected work.

diagrams.title: Four Core Seats, Six at Scale
diagrams.subtitle: 2 FT + 2 C core pod; add 1 FT + 1 C for a 3 FT + 3 C scaled pod.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Numeric values show core-seat occupancy: four values of one and two expansion values of zero. The core comprises 2 FT + 2 C; activating both expansion seats produces 3 FT + 3 C, six people total. Contractor seats represent individual capacity commitments, not guaranteed full-time employee equivalents. External vendor and trade sub-crews are direct subcontractor/COGS pass-through, not internal pod headcount.
diagrams.caption: Conservative and Base scenarios use the four-person core; the Scaled scenario uses all six seats. Consolidate operating responsibilities within the core before expansion, and verify worker classification from actual working arrangements.

stages.label: FT 1: Owner-manager and estimator
stages.value: Core employee seat; commercial and scope accountability
stages.detail: Own pricing, cash forecasting, jurisdiction selection, Xactimate estimates, measured quantities, and supplement support. Escalate contractual disputes appropriately without negotiating policy coverage or claim settlement.

stages.label: FT 2: Project and mitigation lead
stages.value: Core employee seat; field delivery, safety, and quality
stages.detail: Coordinate dispatch and trades, direct extraction and drying, verify psychrometric records and hazard controls, review job costs, and confirm completion before billing. Maintain required qualifications for assigned work.

stages.label: C 1: Mitigation technician
stages.value: Core contractor seat; extraction and monitoring capacity
stages.detail: Perform agreed extraction, equipment handling, moisture monitoring, and containment tasks within documented qualifications and the project's hazard-control plan. Record equipment checks and removal evidence.

stages.label: C 2: Dispatch and receivables coordinator
stages.value: Core contractor seat; scheduling and billing support
stages.detail: Coordinate arrivals, maintain authorization records, prepare invoices, track aging, and reconcile cleared payments under the agreed service scope. The owner-manager retains commercial accountability and approval authority.

stages.label: FT 3: Safety and quality lead
stages.value: Expansion employee seat; core occupancy zero
stages.detail: Activate at scale to audit hazard controls, training, field records, and rework. The project and mitigation lead retains these responsibilities before this hire.

stages.label: C 3: Reconstruction coordinator
stages.value: Expansion contractor seat; core occupancy zero
stages.detail: Activate at scale to coordinate qualified trade vendors, approved repair scopes, moisture acceptance criteria, and completion records. External trade sub-crews remain direct subcontractor/COGS pass-through, not pod seats.

diagrams.title: Startup Capital: A $45,000 Reference Plan
diagrams.subtitle: Four buckets total $45,000 within the $18,000–$75,000 USD range.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Numeric values encode the $45,000 central/reference startup allocation in USD. Details also provide complete $18,000 lean and $75,000 expanded allocations across the same four buckets. Startup capital is funding capacity, not revenue or an immediate operating expense. Choose equipment access and job commitments to fit available funding.
diagrams.caption: Lean: $7,000 + $5,000 + $2,000 + $4,000 = $18,000. Reference: $18,000 + $12,000 + $6,000 + $9,000 = $45,000. Expanded: $30,000 + $20,000 + $10,000 + $15,000 = $75,000.

stages.label: Working-capital reserve
stages.detail: Lean $7,000; reference $18,000; expanded $30,000. Fund receivable delays and job commitments. Model cash needs against the $4,000–$20,000 monthly operating expense planning range and separately fund variable direct job costs; a reserve does not guarantee runway through the 1–5 month time-to-first-deal window.

stages.label: Mitigation equipment
stages.detail: Lean $5,000; reference $12,000; expanded $20,000. Prioritize extraction, air movement, dehumidification, moisture meters, protective equipment, and calibrated measurement tools. Use rental access or suitable used equipment where needed and rent overflow capacity.

stages.label: Vehicle and mobilization setup
stages.detail: Lean $2,000; reference $6,000; expanded $10,000. Fund vehicle rental or lease deposits, secure storage, load restraint, and initial mobilization equipment. Lean deployment assumes access to a suitable existing or rented vehicle; ongoing costs remain operating expenses.

stages.label: Business and technical setup
stages.detail: Lean $4,000; reference $9,000; expanded $15,000. Fund licensing, training, insurance deposits, estimating setup, dispatch configuration, bookkeeping systems, and initial referral development. Limit launch scope to work supported by funded credentials and safeguards.

diagrams.title: Thirty Days to an Operationally Ready Restoration Pod
diagrams.subtitle: Four weekly milestones establish evidence, capacity, and cash controls.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Numeric values are milestone end days. The canonical time to first deal is 1–5 months; this sprint establishes readiness and does not assume a paid job within thirty days. Monthly operating costs span $4,000–$20,000 depending on deployment.
diagrams.caption: Use simulated job files until authorized customer work is available; never fabricate loss evidence, invoices, or insurer responses.

stages.label: Days 1-7
stages.detail: Map contractor and remediation credentials, define public-adjusting boundaries, select the startup budget, and build a thirteen-week cash forecast separating operating costs from direct job commitments.

stages.label: Days 8-14
stages.detail: Assign two employee and two contractor core roles, verify qualifications and worker classification, secure equipment access, and document hazard assessment, respiratory protection, and emergency escalation procedures.

stages.label: Days 15-21
stages.detail: Run a simulated water-loss file through dispatch, photo capture, psychrometric readings, Xactimate scope, customer authorization, job-cost coding, and invoice reconciliation; resolve missing evidence before live use.

stages.label: Days 22-30
stages.detail: Contact targeted property managers and referral partners, track the inquiry cohort, and accept only authorized work within capacity. Review weekly cash exposure, receivable aging, safety events, and job contribution.
